reviews.text: Game was really good and promising, sadly its degenerated in later updates. its become a grindfest, and its so RNG dependant if you want to play at higher threat levels (and you need to play at threat level 45 to unlock all ships), that you basically have to just end runs if you dont get absurdly good RNG drops in the first 2 rounds. Many of these types of deck based upgrade systems struggle with bloat (even with rerolls, discards etc), as adding more cards actually makes it harder to play as making a good build becomes harder. This game tries to solve it with a "tag" system where upgrades are supposed to favour the tags you select with ship and weapons (and a bonus), sadly this seems to have very limited impact overall and leaves you almost entirely at the mercy of rolling good or a run being a loss. The upgrade system is also massively grindy now, with 3 layers of upgrades (skills, paragon cores, artifacts), though you can basically ignore the artifacts as in the last 5 runs I've done I've not seen a single one come up (and I cycles one run three times through all bosses). great looks, really responsive, and a whole load of potential sadly let down by grind and rng domination.

a solid, fairly unique roguelike, in it's current state i don't like only few small things about it: idk if it's intentional, but for one of attacks of Hexagunner and Octagonopus aoe attack indicators show radius way smaller than actual attack, which often caught me off-guard. on the last threat levels u often(more so with slow firing weapons like railgun/chain lightning) find ur success being tied to how lucky u get with upgrades in first zone, since if u don't find something good for crowd control, then after 1st boss u basically enter a recurring cycle of: unable to kill enemies efficiently -> can't walk up and collect exp -> slower level up and power gain -> unable to kill enemies efficiently; which eventually makes u underpowered enough to be overwhelmed, though i find it for not so much a gamedesign flaw but a genre as a whole. wouldn't mind a meta upgrade that allows to reroll single lvlup more than once great game overall, excited to see further development

After having beaten it, you can get your money's worth out of this game, and it is fun, BUT the debuffs on the upgrades that you can get really inhibit the kinds of builds you can go, which decrease the overall satisfaction of building towards the end game for me. I'd rather be able to build something that's unbalanced for the sake of being able to build a certain way than making sure things stay even and upping the difficulty through progression, and decreasing the difficulty through out of match purchases that you use the in-game currency from matches to buy stat upgrades. If you don't mind having builds hampered with a slight restriction in playstyle, it has a satisfying gameplay loop with a decent soundtrack, feels great, and it has decent progressions. However, I probably won't be returning to it anytime soon unless some changes are made.

Weaker version of Nova Drift, not nearly as fun in every way. My first gripe is having talents that are ONLY beneficial in multiplayer mode. There are three or four, and they offer ZERO benefit in Single player. How difficult would it really be to attach a singleplayer ability to that skill as well? Instead you have complete deadspace in the skill tree if you are not playing with somebody else. Incredibly lazy. Lets talk about the skills themselves. There is nothing interesting there at all, it is all stuff like reduce shop prices, add a gambler, add a recycler, add a third shop, add a fourth shop, ALL the skills are like this nothing directly relates to your power as a player. The abilities you pick up during gameplay are so similar as well. Increase movement by 3% or 1% chance to heal on hit, they are such tiny tiny miniscule buffs that you dont ever feel like you are getting stronger. Oh, and all these skills will come with a downside too. You want 3% speed well that comes with -10% defence. Also literally every other skill is focused on damage over time, like literally every other skill. You have to try VERY hard AND get lucky to have a build that ISNT a DoT build. There are very very few raw power upgrades, and like I said they all come with ridiculous downsides. Piggybacking off the multiplayer, the game is very clearly made for more than one player at a time. So why market it as a single player game as well? Sure, you can play in single player, but I guarantee you are not going to have a good time, because everything is built around having two players present. There are A TON of enemies constantly spawning right on top of you, and each time you get hit it takes a third of your health. It seems like the developer didnt even play their own game, because the numbers are just so far off the mark in singleplayer it makes for a very unenjoyable experience. The games does a lot of things "okay", a few things really bad, and nothing exceptional. Developers should decide if they want a single player game or a multiplayer game, instead of trying to shoehorn both into one game and making it so unenjoyable.I will stick to Nova Drift, much cleaner, much better in every way.

This pains me a bit because I've had some fun with this game and there's potential for a solid fusion of Geometry Wars and Vampire Survivors, but the balance is absolutely all over the place. Progression is way too gradual resulting in it taking a LOT of runs to get the power creep snowball rolling. Weapons are a mess as far as balance as well, a handful of them are infuriating to use due to short range when later bosses really can't have you sitting on top of them to hit meaning once you win a run with them you'll never use them again, meanwhile a couple weapons like the cryo-beam are so powerful it's a no-brainer to use them for most runs. The Paragon tree really helps help you not feel underpowered overall but you don't get access to it till you've put a staggering 35 levels into the skill tree, with many unlocks in that being incredibly situational or outright useless or bad to take. If you're good with a loooooong grind to build up in power this game can be a lot of fun. But you're going to have to spend a good 5-10 hours feeling completely weak and useless even once you've learned enemy and boss patterns before it becomes enjoyable, and a lot of people really aren't going to stick around that long out of frustration with the early game.

This is a difficult one and I wish there was a neutral option. I am choosing to downvote for now because this game has fascinating build potential but far too much RNG as you unlock more upgrades. Many of the early upgrades are boring but useful, while most of the later ones are very fun and can even be build defining--if you ever get them. There's a lot of times you can end up rolling tons of upgrades that ONLY work if you first have a way to apply X status or trigger Y effect, but you might just never get offered a good way to trigger/apply said effects reliably (or occasionally, you won't get offered them at all). At higher difficulties, the game just becomes grinding for infinite stat points rather than strategy, and I've personally only been able to get through with retaliation/healing/ice builds, assuming I'm offered sufficient healing to do so. Some of the later weapons are quite interesting and mix it up, like the lightning 'hammer' one (AoE slow firing cone that first shorter>medium>longer>shorter>medium>longer attacks in that order and does very high damage) or the cryo beam (perfect accuracy laser that applies cold). However, many of the weapons can simply become rather useless and almost unimportant to your build without having much way to improve them because again, the upgrade selection is so RNG heavy. Even with 5 rerolls, 5 bans, 5 locks, 5 alters, 1 dual pick, and potentially a small number of additional bits of those added later, the upgrades are just BLOATED. To make things worse, several upgrades suck unless you stack them, requiring even more build focus to get any value out of them! My most successful strategies tend to be just throwing everything possible at the wall, but that invalidates mods you get like Singularity where you do more damage against targets with only one status on them, meaning you still have bloat. I want to keep unlocking things, but I also don't, because it'll make it even harder to get the things I may need. For a game with so much interesting build potential, this is a disappointment. Hopefully they update it with even more control over your upgrade deck--it'd become more tactical and less luck based then. Additionally, the game starts off SLOW right now, which may harm player retention and interest early on--speeding up some of the early levels or just flat out making players start with certain meta upgrades would be a good move. Overall, I'm hopeful for this game, but struggle to recommend it just yet. Still, this is closer to a neutral, and is more just hoping that the devs better tread the fine line between player control and randomness. I'll probably still play it, but it's just so frustrating to go multiple runs without being able to make entire swaths of upgrade combinations work.

I'm honesly flabbergasted. How can a full release feel worse than the early access version? And not even on some deep, systemic way - no, it's the little things that were already working great and somehow got worse. I've been playing since early 2024, and THAT game hooked me - the smooth, neon-geometric style, the grind, the fun. Then came a major update where you introduce Constructs and started shifting away from that clean aesthetic - which was a bit of a mess, sure, but still enjoyable. But 1.0 release? It's rough. Rougher than EA. The flow is gone. Everything feels janky. Even just moving between menu screens feels sharp and abrupt. That arena spawn animation? Absolutely unnecessary and visually exhausting. The constant screen shaking and micro-vibrations even when you're not taking damage - what was that decision about? Add to that over-the-top FX spam in combat and you've got a sensory overload that kills the vibe. And for the love of all gods - WHY ON EARTH DID YOU REDO THE UPGRADE SCREEN? It was perfect. Minimal, elegant, readable - now it's a catastrophe. I've put in over 800 hours, was still enjoying the grind, trying out different builds, and aiming to complete all the achievements. But after this full release, i don't feel it. If refunds were possible at this stage, i'd seriously think about it.

THE GAME HAS SERIOUS PERFORMANCE ISSUES THAT NEED TO BE ADDRESSED, ELSE REVIEW WOULD'VE BEEN POSITIVE I played on the steam deck but I'm sure what I'm observing is not exclusive to the deck. SSF is one of those games where your build can spiral completely out of control since it features endless looping (with increasing enemy count and power) and powerups. This on its own is fine, and it's expected that at some point the amount of action overwhelms CPU/GPU capacity. But it also has a heat/NG+ mechanic ("threat level") which even at a moderate setting (threat level 25) causes FPS to drop to 1-2 on the first loop for multiple seconds. Not a gut feeling, measured with the performance overlay. This is completely unacceptable as you're immobile during those lag spikes and if you aren't filled to the gills with healing perks your run just ends at this point. As it doesn't happen with all builds and the game generally runs very smooth I'm sure this is an issue specific to certain parts of the game code and can be fixed. Sometimes the game also comes to a complete standstill even when not much is going on (the developer in me thinks: maybe a GC pause?). Also easily a run ender. So devs please get your act together because the game is really good otherwise! Geometry wars fans will feel right at home and still get gameplay that's unique enough to not just be a copy of GW. Lots of different enemies and fun bosses, the glowy over the top graphics we know and love, plenty perks and ships/guns to keep you entertained for a long time, at least in the early game. I do have some minor gripes: - unfair bosses: some attack patterns literally cannot be dodged because they are faster than your ship or bigger than the dodge range. Others are just too random (especially the final bosses) to git gud - essentially you gotta go big on healing in order to complete multiple loops. - needs more audio or visual cues, I certainly don't want to check the overlay in the corner to see if my dodges have recharged, or health is getting critical. - in the late game builds pretty much converge to "deal every type of damage on hit, apply healing and hope for the best". Not a huge problem but more than 4 loops usually aren't very entertaining. - way too many perks that aren't viable (too little upsides or substantial downsides). - some text is absolutely microscopic, barely legible on steam deck. - field of view is too restricted, camera needs to zoom out more (could be a button trigger) - music is kinda mid but eh, it's fine.

Easily one of the best mindless grind roguelikes I've come across. There is a huge variety in viable builds, especially as you unlock more stuff, and the difficulty actually feels pretty reasonable. There's a good spike with the threat levels, and a lot of deaths are due to skill or poor build more than anything RNG-based. Whenever I'm feeling bored and want something simple that still feels fun/challenging, this game always comes to mind.

This game deserved a lot more success than it got. The visuals are great and despite being busy in the more hectic moments, I rarely got "lost" in the mix. The tag system is really well done and dramatically improves the roguelike elements over similar titles, allowing you to promote and blacklist tags and giving you a well-balanced level of control of your upgrades against the massive library of choices. I've got a lot of bullet heaven titles in my collection, and this one is hands-down my favorite. Hope more people get a chance to play it.
